{{nihongo|'''Yanahime Shrine'''|矢奈比売神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tōtōmi Province]].

[[File:Yanahime_Jinja_Ichinotorii.jpg|250px|thumb|{{center|First torii}}]]
'''Yanahime Shrine''' (やなひめじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Mitsuke, {{ill|Iwata, Shizuoka|Q386651|qid=Q386651}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It is an {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki-listed minor shrine}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}. It is commonly known as '''Mitsuke Tenjin''' (みつけてんじん).

=== Enshrined deities ===
=== Principal deity ===
*'''Yanahime-no-Ōkami'''
According to '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|Q11588824|qid=Q11588824}},' she is identified as Yano-Wakahime-no-Mikoto.

=== History ===
The date of founding is unknown. The earliest literary record appears in '{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}},' which states that in the 6th month of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 7 ({{ill|840|Q29936|qid=Q29936}}), the shrine was granted the divine rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. In {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 2 ({{ill|860|Q24714|qid=Q24714}}), on {{ill|January 17|Q2264|qid=Q2264}}, it was promoted to Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade. In the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}},' it is listed as a minor shrine.

In {{ill|Shōryaku|de|Shōryaku|fa|شوریاکو|fr|Ère Shōryaku|ia|Shoryaku|id|Shōryaku|ja|正暦|ko|쇼랴쿠|ru|Сёряку|simple|Shōryaku|sr|Шорјаку|tr|Shōryaku|uk|Сьоряку|zh|正曆 (日本)|zh_yue|正曆 (日本)|qid=Q1324858}} 4 ({{ill|993|Q24080|qid=Q24080}}), {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005|lt=Sugawara-no-Ōkami}} was ritually invited from {{ill|Dazaifu Tenmangū|Q710786|qid=Q710786}}, and thereafter the shrine was revered and known as "the Tenjin of Mitsuke" or "Mitsuke Tenjin." In {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 8 ({{ill|1603|Q6735|qid=Q6735}}), {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}} donated a divine estate of 50 koku to the shrine. It served as the tutelary shrine of {{ill|Mitsuke-juku|Q782144|qid=Q782144}}, one of the post stations along the {{ill|53 Stations of the Tōkaidō|Q3134262|qid=Q3134262}}.

=== Legend of the Spirit Dog Shippeitarō ===
{{see also|しっぺい太郎|光前寺#早太郎説話}}
[[File:Reiken Shippeitarou Douzou.jpg|200px|thumb|right|{{center|Bronze statue of the spirit dog Shippeitarō}}]]
[[File:Yanahime Reiken Jinja.jpg|250px|thumb|right|{{center|Reiken Shrine}}]]
This legend is told at this shrine and in various other locations throughout Japan, and its content follows a common pattern. The name Shippeitarō (しっぺいたろう) varies by region; at {{ill|Kōzen-ji|Q11388300|qid=Q11388300}}, the birthplace of Shippeitarō, he is called Hayatarō (はやたろう).

In the village of Mitsuke, every year at the beginning of August, a white-feathered arrow would come flying from an unknown source and lodge itself in the roof of a house. The household struck by the arrow was designated the "year-duty house," and was required to place a daughter alive into a coffin and offer her at Mitsuke Tenjin at midnight on August 10. The offered maiden would be devoured by a monstrous deity that appeared amid earth-shaking tremors. If this custom was broken, the fields would be ruined and the village would suffer famine, so the villagers tearfully upheld the practice.

In the 8th month of {{ill|Enkyō (Kamakura period)|Q1327068|qid=Q1327068|lt=Enkyō}} 1 ({{ill|1308|Q5723|qid=Q5723}}), a wandering monk called an {{ill|Bhikkhu|Q854997|qid=Q854997|lt=unsui}} passed through the post station of Mitsuke and encountered this festival. Noticing that the villagers wore sorrowful expressions despite what should have been a joyful occasion, he inquired and learned of the custom. The unsui, doubting that the tutelary deity of Mitsuke could commit such evil, went to the shrine on the night of the festival and hid himself. What appeared was not a deity but a terrifying monster, which chanted, "Do not tell Shippeitarō of Shinano about this. Tonight, tonight, do not let Shippeitarō know of this!" and carried off the maiden together with the coffin.

To defeat the monster, the unsui set out for {{ill|Shinano Province|ckb|پارێزگای شینانۆ|cs|Provincie Šinano|de|Provinz Shinano|eo|Provinco Ŝinano|es|Provincia de Shinano|fa|ولایت شینانو|fr|Province de Shinano|gl|Provincia de Shinano|hak|Shinano-koet|id|Provinsi Shinano|it|Shinano (provincia)|ja|信濃国|knc|Shinano Province|ko|시나노국|lt|Šinano žemė|ms|Wilayah Shinano|nl|Shinano (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Shinano|pt|Província de Shinano|ru|Синано (провинция)|simple|Shinano Province|sk|Šinano (provincia)|sr|Провинција Шинано|th|แคว้นชินาโนะ|tr|Shinano (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сінано|zh|信濃國|zh_min_nan|Sinano-kok|zh_yue|信濃國|qid=Q289250}} seeking the Shippeitarō whom the creature feared. He could find no person by that name, but after persistent searching, he discovered that Shippeitarō was a dog kept at Kōzen-ji in Ina. The unsui explained the situation to the head priest, received permission to borrow the dog, and returned to Mitsuke with Shippeitarō.

By the time he returned, it was already August of the following year, and once again a white-feathered arrow had appeared on the roof of the year-duty house. The unsui consulted with the villagers, and instead of a maiden, placed Shippeitarō in the coffin as the offering. Shippeitarō fought ferociously through the night against the monster that appeared, and splendidly vanquished it. The monster's true form was a "{{ill|hihī|Q4497985|qid=Q4497985}}," a monkey yōkai of great age. The villagers of Mitsuke expressed their heartfelt gratitude for Shippeitarō's valiant deed and copied all six hundred volumes of the Mahaprajnaparamita Sutra, presenting them to Kōzen-ji.

At '''Reiken Shrine''' (れいけんじんじゃ), located in the northern part of the precinct, the spirit dog Shippeitarō is enshrined. The Iwata City PR character "{{ill|Shippei|Q17212154|qid=Q17212154}}" is modeled after Shippeitarō.

Kōzen-ji, the birthplace of Shippeitarō, is located in present-day {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}} {{ill|Komagane, Nagano|Q838684|qid=Q838684}}. Because of this legend, since {{ill|January 12|Q2248|qid=Q2248}} of {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 42 ({{ill|1967|Q2648|qid=Q2648}}), Iwata City and Komagane City have maintained a friendship city relationship.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Mitsuke Tenjin Hadaka Matsuri - Designated {{ill|December 27|Q2800|qid=Q2800}}, {{ill|2000|Q1985|qid=Q1985}}
** A festival centered on the ritual procession (togyo) in which the deity of Yanahime Shrine proceeds to {{ill|Ōmi Kunitama Shrine|Q43594535|qid=Q43594535}}, the {{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}} of {{ill|Tōtōmi|Q11642126|qid=Q11642126}}. It is held on the Saturday and Sunday immediately before the 10th day of the 8th month of the old calendar<ref name="見付天神裸祭"/>.
